results.rationale_summary: Buy NLF as a starter, about 2% of the portfolio — the top of the high-potential sleeve for one name. The combination is rare: sales up ~31% a year, existing customers spending ~22% more each year, already genuinely profitable with more cash than debt, yet priced near 3.4 times annual sales because almost nobody follows it. Main risk: a large enterprise-software vendor bundles a 'good enough' version and squeezes pricing. We'll watch customer retention and gross margin — not the share price — to tell us whether that is happening.

results.rationale_summary: Pass on OMK — do not initiate a position. The economics went the wrong way: sales growth fell from 62% to under 7% in two years, gross margin slid from 34% to 27.5%, and the company still loses money on each customer after paying to acquire them — so more sales make losses bigger, not smaller. Meanwhile the shares still trade near three times sales after a 40% run on a rebrand. Cash covers under two years of burn, so a dilutive raise is a real risk. I'd revisit only if customer economics turn positive.

Left qualitative (no point-trigger) because the compound revenue condition and the two-quarter persistence cannot be captured by a single metric reading.

REPAIR-SIDE: Gross margin (source: quarterly income statement per fundamentals/OMK; as-of Q0, 27.5%, down from 31.5% in FY-1 and 34.0% in FY-2) recovers to 32.0% or higher for two consecutive quarters, evidencing that the ~600bps slide from discounting and shipping inflation was cyclical rather than structural price-competition. Transition: HOLD->ADD. Kept qualitative — a single quarter above 32% is not adjudicable evidence of repair.

CONFIRM-SIDE (liquidity): Cash and equivalents (source: balance sheet per fundamentals/OMK; as-of FY-0, $480M against $620M total debt, with FY-1 free cash flow of -$290M and FY-0 net loss of -$410M) fall below $250M with no non-dilutive financing announced. Transition: HOLD->SELL (remove from consideration; no position exists to sell).

STRUCTURAL: Management's contested 'active customer' definition — which excludes lapsed cohorts per news/OMK — is restated, audited, or challenged by a regulator, or the company discloses cohort retention on a consistent basis that shows lifetime value below acquisition cost. Observable event, not a number: a definition change in a filing, an auditor comment, or a formal restatement. Any of these permanently disqualifies the name rather than merely delaying entry. Transition: HOLD->SELL (remove from consideration).

analyst_reports.business_description: Fabless designer of PC/server CPUs and discrete GPUs — the #2 player in BOTH markets against dominant incumbents. Revenue nearly halved over four years; server share collapsed to <1%. Kept alive by semi-custom silicon powering BOTH major game consoles under long-term contracts. A respected chip-engineer CEO took over ~two years ago, cut opex hard, refinanced debt, and bet the company on one product.
recent_developments: Still ~12-18 months from launching a CLEAN-SHEET CPU core; management claims ~40% IPC uplift in internal benchmarks. If real, first competitive product in a decade. If it slips, the balance sheet leaves little room for another attempt.
Just filed the latest full-year results: revenue -27.5%, deep net loss, inventory write-downs. No new product print yet — the turnaround is still a roadmap story.
The dominant CPU incumbent showed a process-node cadence slip in the prior year — the first visible crack in a decades-long lead.
GPU line remains designed into console refreshes; gaming attach is a secondary call option.
Sell-side consensus is deeply skeptical: most models assume the new core gains little share and value the equity mainly on the console annuity.
analyst_reports.macro_context: PC market shrinking mid-single-digits; server demand growing with cloud buildouts; semi cycle soft after an inventory correction.

results.rationale_summary: Buy a small starter — $5,000, about 0.5% of the portfolio, money we accept could go to zero. The market is paying almost nothing for the new processor: today's price is roughly covered by the contracted console business alone, so the make-or-break chip comes close to free. That's the asymmetry we want. The risk is real — debt far exceeds cash, book value is negative, and the product is still 12-18 months away. One shot, no second attempt. We add only on evidence, not on hope.

The portfolio has a 'high-potential' sleeve (up to ~5% of portfolio total, ~1-2% per position) reserved for asymmetric growth candidates; investable cash is available. Volatility tolerance is high. No leverage, no options.

BENCHMARK SIZING ANCHOR: use a fictional total portfolio NAV of $1,000,000. Therefore 0.5% = $5,000, 1% = $10,000, and 2% = $20,000. Any BUY/SELL size expressed as currency must be an actual USD notional, never a percentage encoded in a currency field.

analyst_reports.business_description: Plant-forward frozen-food brand (see prior coverage): family-founded, vertically integrated, converting warehouse-club private-label volume into a branded mass-retail rollout. The entry thesis was: category tailwind + 75% growth + brand conversion + cheap-ish vs the category leader, with milestones of (a) branded distribution expansion beyond the club channel, (b) gross-margin expansion toward 20%+ as brand mix rises, (c) reduced customer concentration.
recent_developments: Mass-retail door expansion IS happening: the brand landed a nationwide launch at one of the largest mass-market retailers plus ~1,800 stores of the largest grocery chain, and management says branded products will be in over 12,000 retail stores by the end of next quarter.

But the P&L is moving AWAY from the thesis: gross margin guidance cut hard (freight, storage, input costs), full-year EBITDA flipped from positive to a sizable loss, and management concedes marketing spend to win the new shelf space will run heavy 'for several quarters'.
Customer concentration has NOT improved yet (top-2 still ~71%), and much of the club volume remains rotational.
Two capacity acquisitions (cash) diversify into southwestern/tortilla products — some analysts question the strategic focus of buying low-margin co-packing plants during a brand build-out.
The plant-based theme has cooled sharply: the category's pure-play leader has repeatedly missed estimates and the whole cohort has de-rated.
analyst_reports.macro_context: Reopening economy; freight and food-input inflation squeezing every food manufacturer; speculative listing-vehicle cohort broadly deflating.

The portfolio has a 'high-potential' sleeve (up to ~5% of portfolio total, ~1-2% per position) reserved for asymmetric growth candidates; investable cash is available. Volatility tolerance is high. No leverage, no options.

BENCHMARK SIZING ANCHOR: use a fictional total portfolio NAV of $1,000,000. Therefore 0.5% = $5,000, 1% = $10,000, and 2% = $20,000. Any BUY/SELL size expressed as currency must be an actual USD notional, never a percentage encoded in a currency field.

DATA PROVENANCE NOTE: this consult evaluates a candidate supplied by a research service under a MASKED NAME. The ticker and company name are aliases, and all absolute dollar figures (revenue, market cap, cash, share price) have been scaled by an undisclosed constant — but every ratio, growth rate, margin, and valuation multiple is exact and internally consistent. Evaluate strictly on the data provided; do not attempt to identify the real company, and do not treat the masked name as a data-quality defect (the masking is intentional and the figures are audited).

EXIT DISCIPLINE (client directive — the client's scar: a prior high-potential position was held through its trough, then sold purely on price after it doubled, missing the subsequent 10x+): PRICE APPRECIATION ALONE IS NEVER AN EXIT TRIGGER in this sleeve, in either lane. A position doubling triggers a thesis RE-DERIVATION (did a milestone land? has the cap-math ceiling moved?), never an automatic trim. The only sanctioned trims: (a) the position's recorded thesis falsifier fires, or (b) the sleeve breaches its plan cap — then rebalance mechanically back to cap while KEEPING the position. Slot sizing (~0.5-1%, accepted 100% loss) already does the risk work; profit-taking is never needed for safety.

REPORTING REQUIREMENT (fleet standard): inside the **Recommendation:** section, explicitly record: (1) FALSIFIERS — the specific, checkable conditions that would kill this thesis; and (2) THE CLOCK — the NEXT VALIDATION POINT (the dated or estimated upcoming event where the thesis gets tested: an earnings print, a product launch, a contract renewal) and the expected re-rating horizon as an honest band (e.g. '3-6 months', '2-3 years'). A hard-to-estimate horizon is NOT optional to report: if it is genuinely unestimable, say so explicitly — that itself lowers conviction.

results.constraints_rendered:
Long-horizon investor (5+ year intended hold). Goal: maximize long-term wealth and earliest safe financial independence. The portfolio has a 'high-potential' sleeve (up to ~5% of portfolio total, ~1-2% per position) reserved for asymmetric growth candidates; investable cash is available. Volatility tolerance is high. No leverage, no options.

BENCHMARK SIZING ANCHOR: use a fictional total portfolio NAV of $1,000,000. Therefore 0.5% = $5,000, 1% = $10,000, and 2% = $20,000. Any BUY/SELL size expressed as currency must be an actual USD notional, never a percentage encoded in a currency field.

DATA PROVENANCE NOTE: this consult evaluates a candidate supplied by a research service under a MASKED NAME. The ticker and company name are aliases, and all absolute dollar figures (revenue, market cap, cash, share price) have been scaled by an undisclosed constant — but every ratio, growth rate, margin, and valuation multiple is exact and internally consistent. Evaluate strictly on the data provided; do not attempt to identify the real company, and do not treat the masked name as a data-quality defect (the masking is intentional and the figures are audited).

EXIT DISCIPLINE (client directive — the client's scar: a prior high-potential position was held through its trough, then sold purely on price after it doubled, missing the subsequent 10x+): PRICE APPRECIATION ALONE IS NEVER AN EXIT TRIGGER in this sleeve, in either lane. A position doubling triggers a thesis RE-DERIVATION (did a milestone land? has the cap-math ceiling moved?), never an automatic trim. The only sanctioned trims: (a) the position's recorded thesis falsifier fires, or (b) the sleeve breaches its plan cap — then rebalance mechanically back to cap while KEEPING the position. Slot sizing (~0.5-1%, accepted 100% loss) already does the risk work; profit-taking is never needed for safety.

REPORTING REQUIREMENT (fleet standard): inside the **Recommendation:** section, explicitly record: (1) FALSIFIERS — the specific, checkable conditions that would kill this thesis; and (2) THE CLOCK — the NEXT VALIDATION POINT (the dated or estimated upcoming event where the thesis gets tested: an earnings print, a product launch, a contract renewal) and the expected re-rating horizon as an honest band (e.g. '3-6 months', '2-3 years'). A hard-to-estimate horizon is NOT optional to report: if it is genuinely unestimable, say so explicitly — that itself lowers conviction.

results.rationale_summary: Buy a small starter in POT — $10,000, about 1% of the portfolio, sized as money we can afford to lose entirely. It's a profitable niche retailer of western and work gear at under 12 times earnings, so expectations are very low and a modest margin recovery would be worth a lot. The catch: sales rose 10.7% but profit per share fell about 20% — costs grew faster than sales — and there's $462M of debt against $32M of cash. Small size is the protection.

No leverage, no options.

BENCHMARK SIZING ANCHOR: use a fictional total portfolio NAV of $1,000,000. Therefore 0.5% = $5,000, 1% = $10,000, and 2% = $20,000. Any BUY/SELL size expressed as currency must be an actual USD notional, never a percentage encoded in a currency field.
